stem: A 14-year-old is seen alone during a general paediatric review. She says she has never been sexually active but feels increasingly distressed about being attracted to girls and asks whether sexual health even applies to her. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Sexual health includes physical, emotional, mental and social wellbeing related to sexuality, so it is reasonable to talk about how this is affecting you
Sexual health questions are mainly for young people who are already having intercourse
If there is no current STI or pregnancy risk, sexuality concerns sit outside adolescent health care
It is best to defer discussion of sexuality until late adolescence, when identity is more settled
The main purpose of sexual health review is to decide whether contraception is needed

explanation: Sexual health is broader than intercourse or pregnancy prevention. It includes physical, emotional, mental and social wellbeing related to sexuality, so this concern should be explored sensitively in adolescent care.

rationale: Sexual health is broader than intercourse or contraception. Adolescent sexual health includes emotional, mental and social wellbeing. Concerns about sexuality are appropriate to discuss even when there is no immediate STI or pregnancy risk.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because sexual health includes physical, emotional, mental and social wellbeing related to sexuality, not just intercourse or pregnancy prevention.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because sexual health applies beyond young people who are already sexually active.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because sexuality concerns remain part of adolescent health care even without STI or pregnancy risk.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because discussion of sexuality should not be routinely delayed until late adolescence.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because contraception is only one aspect of sexual health, not its main purpose.
